question: The Commissioner responsible for the rule of law, Michael McGrath, issued a statement on the crisis in the Polish Constitutional Tribunal, which Politico described as ‘appearing to support Tusk’s position’. In his statement, the Commissioner referred to the opinion of the Venice Commission1.

The Commission is keen to invoke the authority of the Venice Commission when its positions serve to support Prime Minister Donald Tusk and justify his actions. Meanwhile, when the opinions of the same Venice Commission point out obligations that are inconvenient for Prime Minister Donald Tusk to meet, the Commission remains silent.

In December 2024, the Venice Commission adopted an opinion on the obligation to publish the rulings of the Constitutional Tribunal2. Donald Tusk’s government has, for political reasons, failed to publish around 70 judgments of the Constitutional Tribunal. In light of the above: 1.

Why does the Commission remain silent on the enforcement of Venice Commission opinions that are unfavourable to Prime Minister Donald Tusk, while speaking out firmly in the case of Venice Commission opinions that are favourable to him?

Why does the Commission assess the rule of law solely on the basis of an interpretation of the facts that is favourable to politicians associated with the European People’s Party and the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats?

Does the Commission consider the takeover of constitutional institutions through the use of uniformed services and the exclusion of judges not appointed by the current ruling parties to be a manifestation of the rule of law?
